tasks.verify: MEASURED ON THE TRACED SUBTUNE (s0, correspondence s0->o0 92%, voices 0 and 2 both ratio 1.00 / pitches 100%). Voice index 1 is ratio 0.77 / pitches 62%, and the whole of it is ONE note: the original plays **B-5 95 times** and we play **G#7 96 times**, 22 semitones high. Every other note on that voice is exact -- E-4 81/81, G-4 28/28, F-4 16/16, D-4 12/12, G#4 4/4. G#7 is this repo's known CLAMP CEILING (see v0.5.391, '155 of Monty's notes stop clamping to G#7'), so the pitch ran off the top of the note table and was pinned there rather than being transposed. **THE LISTENER SAID 'TOO LOW' AND THE TRACE SAYS TOO HIGH.** Do not assume the trace is right and the ear wrong, and do not assume the reverse: FIRST establish which subtune was heard. Commando has 19 and the pages play the default; a clamped ceiling note in an arpeggio can also be perceived as the figure sitting wrong rather than as one note being high. If the heard subtune is not s0 this row is not the reported defect and a new measurement is needed. DONE WHEN the clamp's cause is found (which transpose or table lookup takes B-5 above the range), the fix keeps every other note on the voice exact, a test pins it, and a corpus byte-hash names exactly the files that move.

tasks.verify: CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY BY A LISTENER, who reported it as a SPEED mismatch -- and the speed is exact: --pace reads our row 3.00 frames, ratio 1.000, IQR 1.000-1.000 over 295 gaps, drift +0.00, '0% out', with melody 100% and 298/298 attacks. It is LENGTH: `len` reads `>+294.9s !`, the corpus's only measured failure of the +-5s rule, against an original that stops at 305.08s. THE CAUSE IS LOCATED AND IS NOT THE $FE PATH. `legalise_restarts` reports **0 restarts changed** on this file, so `--legal-restart` and `--silent-park` (both ON in its presets) have nothing to act on. Its tracks end `$FF` with an operand, and voice 2's reads `FF 4B` -- restart position 75 in a list of about 39. An OUT-OF-RANGE restart is precisely how this project models 'tune ended', so the ending signal is being normalised or clamped away inside convert_tracks before it can reach the .sng. Read the $FF handling in tracks.py against the raw bytes. DONE WHEN Confuzion's `len` lands within the +-5s tolerance, a test pins the $FF-out-of-range reading, and a corpus byte-hash names EXACTLY the files that move -- state the number up front. A $FF rule that moves 40 files is scoped wrongly; that is the lesson the $FD/$FE terminator work already paid for.
